where: the Missing in action rows in the left column, y=358 to the fold and on to y=1510
finding: The frame change gave this card 680px of width and the row did not spend any of it, so the list that is the whole job still arrives four names at a time. Each MIA row is a three-line text block with a fourth line under it holding Call, Text and the phone number, and none of those four lines uses the right half of the row. The leader on a Tuesday morning came to find out whether this is a four-call week or a twelve-call week; the fold answers 'at least four' and makes them scroll for the rest, exactly as it did in round 1. The column split fixed the page and left the row alone — and the row is now the only thing between the leader and all ten names on one screen.
evidence: Left column runs x=256–936 (680px). Rows are 113–118px: dividers at y=358, 476, 589, 711, 836, so Leila, Trevor, Jasmine and Rohan are complete and Ana Lucia's name lands at y=862 with her contact line below the 900px fold — 4 of 10, versus 3.5 of 10 in round 1. On the top line the meta text ends at x=588 and the MISSED badge starts at x=865: 277px of empty row. On the contact line the phone number ends at x=592, leaving 344px. The card is ~1,230px tall for content that measures ~450px wide at its widest point. Below it the Attendance trend runs to y=1890 while the right column has stopped at y=1585, so 448×305px is blank beside it.
direction: Fold the contact line up into the row: name and one meta line on the left, Call/Text and the missed badge pinned right, at roughly 65–70px per row. Ten rows then measure ~700px and the whole list clears the fold under the tiles. The printed phone number is the cheapest thing to drop — Call and Text already carry it, and it is the string that forces the fourth line. Nothing here touches the gathering split or the All/Sunday/Friday filter.

where: the right column — New faces at y=280–580 and Incomplete profiles at y=596 onward, both above the fold
finding: Putting the small lists side by side exposed something the single stacked column had been hiding behind 1,200px of scroll: the same students are in two lists at once, and the two lists prescribe different actions for them. Selah Mbeki and Jayden Rivers appear in New faces with an amber 'Incomplete' badge and a 48px 'Add parent contact' button, and again 320px lower in Incomplete profiles with a 'Waiting 1 day' pill and a chevron. A leader reading down that column to build this week's call list has to work out by name that these are four entries about two people, and that the card literally titled 'Incomplete profiles' is the one that does not offer the fix. Scroll used to make this an inconsistency nobody met; the column makes it a contradiction on the fold, on the screen whose value is that its counts can be trusted.
evidence: Selah Mbeki's name renders at y=376 and again at y=696; Jayden Rivers at y=489 and y=765 — same 448px column, both pairs above the fold. Across the four list sections the page shows 21 entries covering 16 distinct students: Selah and Jayden are in New faces and Incomplete profiles; Trevor Boyd is in MIA (y=499) and Incomplete profiles (y=1019); Bree Sandoval and Tomas Vielle are in Incomplete profiles and in Met once, never since. The tiles above read 10 / 2 / 7, which sums to 19 rows about 14 people.
direction: Decide what a section membership means when a student qualifies for two. Either the smaller card defers ('2 new faces — both already listed under Incomplete profiles'), or the action moves so each person is offered one next step in one place: 'Add parent contact' belongs in the card named after missing contact, and New faces can carry the flag without repeating the row. Do not solve it by re-stacking the columns — the split is the right answer and the duplication was always there.

where: the right-hand Past gatherings column, from the 'Load older gatherings' button at y=1039 down to the bottom of the page at y=2447
finding: The split did its job — three weeks ago is now on the fold instead of 2,500px down — but the two halves are wildly different lengths, so the page trades one kind of emptiness for another. The past column runs out after twelve rows and the upcoming column keeps going for another 1,300px of alternating Friday Fellowship / Sunday School rows out to Sep 20. From the moment the leader scrolls past the first screen, they are reading a 560px list with 560px of flat ink beside it, which is the shape the round-1 critique was about. Nobody's stated job breaks — all three are served on the fold now — but the recurring rows are the bulk of the page and they are the part that got no width.
evidence: Page is 2,447px tall. Right column x=845–1407 (562px); its last row ends at y=1025 and 'Load older gatherings' at y=1039–1083. Left column x=256–816; its last row ends at y=2405. That is 1,322×562px — 54% of the page height with a blank right half. The 16 'Later' rows are 82px each carrying an icon, a title, a date/time/location line and a 'Recurring' badge, for two series that alternate. 'Load older gatherings' — the control for anything before Jun 21 — sits 139px below the 900px fold.
direction: Let the length imbalance be the thing that decides the layout rather than the calendar order. Either the Later group flows into two sub-columns once the past column has ended, or the repeating occurrences collapse to a denser row (one line: date, series, room) so sixteen of them cost 500px instead of 1,300. A month grid is not needed to fix this and was already declined.

where: the directory rows, from y=178 to the bottom of the list at y=2192
finding: The row got shorter without getting denser. It is now 44px tall and 1,152px wide and it carries the same two facts it carried at 65px — a name on the left and a grade pinned at the far right — with about 790px of nothing between them. Sixteen names above the fold instead of nine is a real win for 'find one student among forty-five'; the second clause of the job, 'see who has no parent contact', is still not answerable from the list. The flag exists but it is an inline badge that trails five of the forty-five names at whatever x the name happens to end, so the leader scanning for it is reading a ragged mid-row position rather than a column — in a row that has 790px of unused width sitting right where that column would go.
evidence: Rows are `lg:min-h-11` at a 45px pitch: 200, 245, 290 … 875, sixteen visible before the 900px fold, list ending at y=2192 on a 2,259px page. The name span is `lg:flex-1` (~940px) holding names that measure 100–190px; grade is a fixed `lg:w-28` at x=1266–1378. 'Missing info' badges appear on 5 rows (Bree Sandoval x=510, Jayden Rivers x=443, Kylie Novak x=428, Selah Mbeki x=434, Tomas Vielle x=436) — five different x positions.
direction: Give the flags a fixed column beside the grade so the answer to 'who has no parent contact' is a vertical run rather than a filter click that discards the alphabet. This is a column for a fact already on the row, not a new fact about a minor. If width is still spare after that, two columns of the A–Z list puts all forty-five names on one screen — the roster's 'a tap never moves a row' constraint does not apply here, since a mis-click opens a neighbouring record and costs one Back.
